pr_title: [ActiveStorage] Take `ActiveRecord` affixes into account for `ActiveStorage` database models
pr_body:
EDIT: Partially Fixes #35811 ( Only AR suffix will work, prefix is a global engine issue that will be handled in a separate PR
Follow up to the closed PR #35828 

Follow up to https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/30095

### Motivation / Background

<!--
Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important?
If you are fixing a specific issue, include "Fixes #ISSUE" (replace with the issue number, remove the quotes) and the issue will be linked to this PR.
-->

This Pull Request has been created because ActiveStorage db model table names are hardcoded. Making it impossible to be compatible with ActiveRecord prefix/suffix configuration.

What's also problematic is that AS generated migrations ( with `activestorage:install` task ) respects the prefix/suffix configuration, which makes it then impossible to use AS models in a Rails application.

### Detail

To fix this issue we remove the hard coded lines. But then we need to also override an internal method for specifying the prefix. the full explanation is here: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50167#discussion_r1405175059

### Additional information

Some tests were refactored to remove hard coded table name references, making ActiveStorage test suite compatible with ActiveRecord config.

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/354d68e8a63b21e47a529105a508411bfe8be869/activerecord/lib/active_record/model_schema.rb#L597-L611

- **I believe the root cause lies inside ActiveRecord model schema file** but I can't find the solution... for now ( **EDIT: solution found here: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50167#discussion_r1405175059 )** 
- This issue is also present in action_text, but I want to focus for now on activestorage and make sure it works properly before porting it

pr_comments:
Hi @jonathanhefner sorry for the ping, do you mind having a look at this PR. I believe if this gets approved it can also be ported to ActionText ( and any other action_* rails gem that uses activerecord to generate tables)

Thanks 🙏🏼 
As you mentioned, this seems to affect all engines that use `isolate_namespace`.  Here is a reproduction script of #35811 for an arbitrary engine:

<details>
  <summary>Reproduction script</summary>
  
  ```ruby
  # frozen_string_literal: true

  require "bundler/inline"

  gemfile(true) do
    source "https://rubygems.org"

    git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

    gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
    gem "sqlite3"
  end

  require "rails/all"

  module TestEngine
    class Engine < Rails::Engine
      isolate_namespace TestEngine
    end

    class Record < ActiveRecord::Base
    end
  end

  class TestApp < Rails::Application
    config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f

    config.root = __dir__
    config.hosts << "example.org"
    config.eager_load = false
    config.session_store :cookie_store, key: "cookie_store_key"
    config.secret_key_base = "secret_key_base"

    config.logger = Logger.new($stdout)
    Rails.logger  = config.logger

    config.active_record.table_name_prefix = "abc_"
    config.active_record.table_name_suffix = "_xyz"
  end

  ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = "sqlite3::memory:"

  Rails.application.initialize!

  ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
    create_table :test_engine_records do |t|
      t.string :value
    end
  end

  require "minitest/autorun"

  class EngineTest < Minitest::Test
    def test_record_table_name
      assert_equal "abc_test_engine_records_xyz", TestEngine::Record.table_name
    end

    def test_record
      TestEngine::Record.create!(value: "foo")
      assert_equal "foo", TestEngine::Record.first.value
    end
  end
  ```
</details>

Output:

  ```
  Failure:
  EngineTest#test_record_table_name:
  Expected: "abc_test_engine_records_xyz"
    Actual: "test_engine_records_xyz"

  Error:
  EngineTest#test_record:
  ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: Could not find table 'test_engine_records_xyz'
  ```

There are two important observations:

1. `config.active_record.table_name_suffix` __does__ work.  That implies `config.active_record.table_name_prefix` should also work.  (If neither worked, there would be more of an argument for "that's just the way it is.")

2. Basic Active Record operations __do not__ work at all for engine namespaced models when `config.active_record.table_name_prefix` is set.  This is really important because it means that fixing `table_name_prefix` for engines won't break apps that rely on the existing behavior (because those apps couldn't have worked in the first place).

So, I think it would be better to fix the root cause and address this issue for all engines that use `isolate_namespace`.
@jonathanhefner Thank you for the reproduction script and confirming my theory, and also for the review!

I have a suggestion, if you don't mind, can I just keep the fix regarding the hardcoded table names ( which are redundant since they're already covered by `isolate_namespace` and non breaking)

And I remove this part and the tests related to it
```ruby
  def self.full_table_name_prefix
    table_name_prefix.to_s + super
  end
```

Then I can try to fix this global issue for all engines in another PR using your reproduction script?🙏🏼 

If it's ok with you, I will first create an issue and use the reproduction script in the description, then I can work on a fix.
> can I just keep the fix regarding the hardcoded table names ( which are redundant since they're already covered by `isolate_namespace` and non breaking)

It looks like `isolate_namespace` was added later in #30095, which is why the table names were originally hard-coded.  So, as a follow-up to #30095, removing them seems fine.

> If it's ok with you, I will first create an issue and use the reproduction script in the description, then I can work on a fix.

Sounds good. :+1:
@jonathanhefner I believe this PR is ready. As discussed above, I went ahead and created the issue https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/50246

Again, thanks for your time.
Thank you, @chaadow! :card_file_box:

Backported to `7-1-stable` in 29cc70858d7bddeae71ce036090fe407b1552d1c.

issue_context.title: Active Storage models ignore table_name_prefix
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
1. `rails new astest`
2. `cd astest/`
3. Edit `config/application.rb` and add set a general table prefix with `config.active_record.table_name_prefix = 'abc_'`
4. Create ActiveStorage models `bundle exec rake active_storage:install db:migrate`

Observe: tables are created with prefix (`abc_active_storage_attachements` and `*_blobs`).

5. Create a user model via `bundle exec rails generate model User name:string` and attach an avatar to it
```
class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_one_attached :avatar
end
```
6. Add an Avatar via console
```
2.6.1 :002 > u.avatar.attach(io: File.open(Rails.root.join('public', 'apple-touch-icon.png')))
Traceback (most recent call last):
        1: from (irb):2
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid (Could not find table 'active_storage_attachments')
```

Observe: ActiveRecord cannot find its table.

### Expected behavior
ActiveStorage::Attachment should use the prefixed table name the migration created previously.

### Actual behavior
ActiveStorage::Attachment cannot find its table as it looks for the non-prefixed table name.

Which is hardcoded in ActiveStorage::Attachment [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/d2542882b20f6205e1c40ab34ff075eefc2d589c/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/attachment.rb#L9) and in ActiveStorage::Blob [here](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/d2542882b20f6205e1c40ab34ff075eefc2d589c/activestorage/app/models/active_storage/blob.rb#L27)

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 5.2.3
**Ruby version**: 2.6.1
comments:
I tried reproducing this issue but the migration generated for Active Storage tables have correct names.

<details>

``` rb
cat db/migrate/20190401081542_create_active_storage_tables.active_storage.rb
# This migration comes from active_storage (originally 20170806125915)
class CreateActiveStorageTables < ActiveRecord::Migration[5.2]
  def change
    create_table :active_storage_blobs do |t|
      t.string   :key,        null: false
      t.string   :filename,   null: false
      t.string   :content_type
      t.text     :metadata
      t.bigint   :byte_size,  null: false
      t.string   :checksum,   null: false
      t.datetime :created_at, null: false

      t.index [ :key ], unique: true
    end

    create_table :active_storage_attachments do |t|
      t.string     :name,     null: false
      t.references :record,   null: false, polymorphic: true, index: false
      t.references :blob,     null: false

      t.datetime :created_at, null: false

      t.index [ :record_type, :record_id, :name, :blob_id ], name: "index_active_storage_attachments_uniqueness", unique: true
      t.foreign_key :active_storage_blobs, column: :blob_id
    end
  end
end
```
</details>

Here is the repro app https://github.com/prathamesh-sonpatki/rails-35811/blob/master/config/application.rb#L19
Not the migration is the issue, the AS tables ARE created correctly, but they cannot be accessed afterwards (see points 5. and 6. above)
Thanks, I am working on a fix.

Just wondering why `active_storage_variant_records` is missed out on this one? Also `active_storage_variant_records` doesn't even have a `run_load_hooks` so overriding anything is much more hacky.

Would you consider adding both of these things and releasing this in the 6.1 series?
It seems like @prathamesh-sonpatki had a PR but was closed and needs to be rebased since the default branch change. Would you be interested in picking this back up? 🙏

You're right, I misinterpreted things :D

I'll look at adding that extra load hook first, then think about the other problem. The issue is that the default behaviour when setting the table name is for that to override any prefix or affix settings if I understand rightly? The problem is rails is internally using an external API that then makes it hard to override.
Here's the first PR to add the hook: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42307

In terms of the other problem, I've tried: ```ruby class ActiveStorage::Record < ActiveRecord::Base #:nodoc: self.abstract_class = true class << self def model_name ActiveModel::Name.new(self, nil, name.demodulize) end end end ActiveSupport.run_load_hooks :active_storage_record, ActiveStorage::Record ``` All of the existing tests pass except for two that test URL creation. `polymorphic_url` generation relies on the existence of the namespace to namespace the route: ``` undefined method `attachments_url' ``` I think it should be looking for `active_storage_attachments_url`. ``` test "attachment" do attachment = ActiveStorage::Attachment.new(blob: @blob) assert_dom_equal %(), image_tag(attachment) end ``` ``` test "blob" do assert_dom_equal %(), image_tag(@blob) end ``` I'm now trying to find out if there's a way to fix route lookup for a model without messing with the `model_name` itself.

Actually it's as easy as adding:

```
self.table_name_prefix = 'active_storage_'
```

to the abstract base class and removing the explicit table names from the child classes. My current assumption is that this prefix will also be prefixed by the rails application configuration of the same.

Just need to figure out how to test this.

@zzak, this one is getting a bit weird. All the tests pass even after removing the table name declarations, e.g.:

```
self.table_name = "active_storage_blobs"
```

It seems rails already adds `active_storage` because that's the namespace of the model. That'd be fine as it is, but I've now noticed that setting a `table_name_prefix` in `ActiveStorage::Record` doesn't have any effect, but changing it to `table_name_suffix` does work. It's so strange. Makes me feel like it's being overridden from elsewhere.

Even if I put this inside of `ActiveStorage::Blob` itself:

```
self.table_name_prefix = "something_"
```

It still doesn't have any effect. I wonder if the autogenerated module prefix obliterates any other setting? I thought it would append to the prefix.
See: https://github.com/brendon/rails/tree/active-storage-table-name for the change plus a failing test.
This should be re-opened BTW because the other PR didn't fix this particular issue. @pixeltrix

@brendon I'm glad to inform you that I've solved the mystery of why setting the prefix has no effect, while setting the suffix works. the explanation is here! : https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/50167#discussion_r1405175059
Thanks @chaadow, good investigation! :) Now if only I could remember why I needed this :D

review_comments: this follows the logic that table names should not be hard coded
